# Starting voice and editorial style

This is a suggested default, adapted from the original team's writing preferences. It is not an approved brand voice for your company. Keep what fits and refine it using your own published work.

## How the writing should feel
- Plain, direct and practical. Write as one knowledgeable person helping another.
- Lead with the useful outcome. Give enough context for someone new to the topic.
- Use active voice and complete sentences. Prefer periods and commas to em dashes.
- Explain unfamiliar terms on first use. Avoid unexplained internal labels.
- Skip hype, dramatic openings, slang and help-desk padding.
- Use concrete examples. Never invent personal experience, customer quotes or results.

## Keep the article separate from the work behind it
Keep research logs, internal checklists and publication blockers beside the draft, not in its body. Still include citations, attribution, disclosures and limitations when they matter to the reader or are required.

Use descriptive headings, short paragraphs and comparisons that help a real decision. Let the topic determine length. Drafts remain drafts until reviewed and approved.

## Make it yours
Share two or three examples you like and anything you want to avoid. The agent should propose a tailored voice from those examples rather than ask you to write a full style guide.
